speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and do you have any awareness of them afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

text: The EEG findings of right temporal lobe spikes, combined with the olfactory aura (muddy taste) and automatisms, strongly point to a specific type of seizure. Do you have any history of head trauma, fever, or recent infections that might have triggered this onset?

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the temporal lobe EEG findings and the specific aura, the clinical picture is consistent with focal impaired awareness seizures. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
